mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares the number of intersection points in Configuration A (three lines all pass through the same point) and Configuration B (each pair of the three lines meets at a different point)?

options.A: Both configurations have the same number of intersection points.
options.B: Configuration A has fewer intersection points than Configuration B.
options.C: Configuration A has more intersection points than Configuration B.
options.D: Configuration A has no intersection points.

mcqs.answer: Configuration A has fewer intersection points than Configuration B.
mcqs.explanation: When three lines are concurrent (Configuration A) they share a single common point, giving only 1 intersection point. When each pair meets at a different point (Configuration B) there are 3 distinct intersection points (AB, BC, CA). Hence Configuration A has fewer intersection points.

mcqs.question: Line L1: y = x + 2, Line L2: y = -2x + 5, and Line L3: y = x + 2 are drawn on the same coordinate plane. Which point is an intersection point of the distinct lines?
mcqs.explanation: L1 and L3 are the same line, so the only distinct pair is L1 (or L3) with L2. Solving x + 2 = -2x + 5 gives 3x = 3, so x = 1 and y = 3. Thus the unique intersection point of the distinct lines is (1, 3). The other options are not solutions of the equations.

mcqs.question: When three different lines intersect at a single point, how many angles are formed at that point?
mcqs.explanation: Each line creates two opposite (vertical) angles with the other two lines. With three lines, the point is divided into six angles, each pair of opposite angles being equal. Therefore, six angles are formed.

mcqs.question: Which description matches three lines that intersect pairwise but not all at the same point?

options.A: All three lines meet at one point.
options.B: Two lines are parallel and the third cuts them.
options.C: Each line meets the other two at different points.

mcqs.answer: Each line meets the other two at different points.
mcqs.explanation: When no two lines are parallel and no three are concurrent, each pair meets at its own distinct point, giving three different intersection points. Option C describes exactly this arrangement.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines "concurrent lines" and distinguishes them from "non‑concurrent lines"?

options.A: Concurrent lines intersect at a single point; non‑concurrent lines intersect at three different points.
options.B: Concurrent lines are parallel; non‑concurrent lines are intersecting.
options.C: Concurrent lines intersect pairwise; non‑concurrent lines are coincident.
options.D: Concurrent lines are the same line; non‑concurrent lines are different.

mcqs.answer: Concurrent lines intersect at a single point; non‑concurrent lines intersect at three different points.
mcqs.explanation: Three lines are called concurrent when they all pass through one common point. If they are not concurrent, each pair meets at a separate point, giving three distinct intersections. Option A captures this definition accurately.

mcqs.question: Line A and line B intersect at point P. Line C is drawn through point P as well. How many distinct intersection points are there among the three lines?
mcqs.explanation: All three lines share the same common point P. Although each pair of lines meets, they all meet at the same location, so there is only one distinct intersection point.

mcqs.question: In a diagram three lines intersect at point O, creating angles of 30°, 70°, 80°, 30°, 70°, and 80°. Which statement is true?

options.A: The sum of all angles is 360°.

mcqs.answer: The sum of all angles is 360°.
mcqs.explanation: The six angles around a point always add up to 360°. Adding 30 + 70 + 80 + 30 + 70 + 80 = 360°, confirming option A. The other statements are false: there are no right angles, the largest angle is 80° (acute), and there are no obtuse angles.

mcqs.question: A student draws three lines: line 1 is horizontal, line 2 slants upward and crosses line 1, and line 3 is drawn parallel to line 1. Which description best fits this arrangement?

options.A: All three lines intersect at a single point.
options.B: Two lines are parallel and the third cuts them.
options.C: Each line meets the other two at different points.

mcqs.answer: Two lines are parallel and the third cuts them.
mcqs.explanation: Line 1 and line 3 are parallel, so they never meet. Line 2 intersects both of them, acting as a transversal. Hence the arrangement matches option B. The other options do not reflect the given relationships.
